jobs_results.job_title: Quality Assurance Engineer II, Amazon Robotics Systems Quality and Performance Engineering
jobs_results.description:
Description

Are you passionate about quality and robotics? Do you thrive on solving complex problems that span hardware, software, and system integration? Amazon Robotics is looking for a Quality Assurance Engineer II to own quality for robotic systems deployed across Amazon's fulfillment network.

In this role, you won't just execute test plans — you'll define them. You'll take ambiguous product requirements and turn them into comprehensive test strategies covering functional, integration, and performance testing. You'll work hands-on with robotic systems on our test floors, validating that releases meet the quality bar before they reach production sites. When you find problems, you won't just file a bug — you'll trace the root cause across system boundaries and give developers the evidence they need to fix it fast.

You'll also build tools and automation that make the whole team more effective — scripting repeatable test scenarios, developing methods to evaluate release quality, and creating documentation that lets teammates run your tests independently. Your work will multiply the impact of everyone around you. You'll collaborate daily with software engineers, hardware engineers, and systems engineers, representing quality in design reviews, release decisions, and cross-team discussions.

This is a hands-on role based at our BOS27 facility in Westborough, MA. If you want to work at the intersection of robotics, quality engineering, and real-world impact, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end test strategy for robotic features and systems — defining what to test, how to test it, and what infrastructure is needed, even when requirements are ambiguous or evolving.

Create and execute test plans for complex test scenarios including system integration, robotic workcell validation, and safety-critical functionality across hardware, software, and firmware boundaries.

Design and build automated test solutions that are maintainable, reusable, and reliable — enabling other engineers to run and extend them independently.

Develop test strategies for non-functional areas such as performance, reliability, and regression detection to ensure product quality is measured objectively.

Isolate, document, and validate defects with detailed evidence and root-cause analysis, enabling development teams to triage and resolve issues efficiently.

Represent quality assurance in cross-functional discussions including design reviews, release readiness decisions, and retrospectives — advocating for quality at every stage of the development lifecycle.

Collaborate with software developers, hardware engineers, and systems engineers to understand technical architecture and assess how changes impact test scope and product behavior.

Mentor junior engineers, interns, and contractors — training them on products, test methodologies, and tools, and creating documentation that reduces tribal knowledge.

Execute testing on physical test floors to qualify releases prior to production deployment, working directly with robotic systems and workcells.

Proactively identify quality risks, propose solutions, and take on projects that improve testing processes or more accurately measure product quality.

A day in the life

Your day starts with a team standup where you and your fellow QA engineers level set on priorities, blockers, and what's happening across active test campaigns. From there, your day might look different depending on where you are in a release cycle.

Some days are heavily hands-on — you're on the test floor at BOS27 running test scenarios against robotic workcells, capturing logs, and investigating unexpected behavior. You'll troubleshoot across hardware, software, and firmware boundaries, pulling data from multiple sources to build a clear picture of what went wrong and why.

Other days are more collaborative — you're in design reviews with software and hardware engineers, asking the questions that shape how a feature gets tested. You might be scoping a test strategy for a new capability, defining what "done" looks like when the requirements are still evolving, or presenting release analysis to stakeholders who need a clear verdict on whether a build is ready for production.

In between, you're building — writing test cases, developing automation that your teammates can pick up and run, creating documentation that eliminates the need for someone to tap you on the shoulder every time. You'll also spend time mentoring junior engineers and contractors, helping them ramp on products and test approaches.

You'll regularly collaborate with software development engineers, systems engineers, hardware engineers, and program managers. Your internal customers are the development teams who depend on your test results to make release decisions, and the operations teams who rely on the quality of what ships to fulfillment sites.

In this role you will work at the intersection of machine learning and physical robotics hardware. You will collaborate with hardware engineers to evaluate how your models perform on real sensors and edge compute, run experiments that directly influence what gets built next, and validate perception systems alongside robotics program teams. You will push the boundaries of computer vision for robotic applications while seeing your work deploy on real robots in real fulfillment centers. This is applied science with immediate, measurable impact at a scale no other robotics company can offer.

Amazon offers a full range of benefits that support you and eligible family members, including domestic partners. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:

 Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage Maternity and Parental Leave Options Paid Time Off (PTO) 401(k) Plan

If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you! At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!

About The Team

The Amazon Robotics Quality Assurance Engineering team is a group of approximately 20 engineers supporting a broad portfolio of robotic products and solutions — from manipulation systems and autonomous mobile robots to sortation, storage and retrieval, and outbound dock automation. Our work spans first mile, middle mile, last mile, and outbound dock operations across Amazon's fulfillment network.

We operate across three major test sites in Massachusetts — BOS12 (North Reading), BOS27 (Westborough), and BOS33 (Woburn) — where we maintain dedicated test floors with real robotic workcells and integration environments. We are a mix of hands-on testers, automation builders, and quality strategists who work closely with software, hardware, and systems engineering teams to make sure what ships to production actually works. We are growing and looking for curious, technically strong people who want to make a real impact on how robotics technology serves customers worldwide.

Basic Qualifications

 4+ years of quality assurance engineering experience Experience in automation testing Experience in manual testing Experience as QA lead on medium to large sized projects

Preferred Qualifications

 Experience with at least one automated test framework like Selenium or Appium Experience in gathering test requirements to create detailed test plans and defining quality metrics to measure product quality Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems Experience developing high quality test plans, test designs, test strategies, and test execution Experience of using test case management tools (e.g. Test Rail, TestLink) and issue management tools (Jira) Experience working closely with development and business teams to communicate problem impacts and to understand business requirements

About Lucid


At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience. 


We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

 






Position Overview




The Powertrain Robotics Engineer, supports robot commissioning, programming, recovery, and tooling integration across AMP-2 Powertrain robotic cells. Joining at facility launch, this engineer supports FANUC, ABB, and KUKA cells from first commissioning through volume ramp. The role is a hands-on contributor to robot uptime, cycle time, and safety compliance.






 






Key Responsibilities


 





Robot Integration, Commissioning, Teaching & Programming for FANUC, ABB, and KUKA
Support offline programming and simulation activities
Maintain and optimize the robots to maximize the throughput throughout the life-cycle of the asset.

Robot Recovery & Troubleshooting



Diagnose robot faults: encoder, drive, cables, controller, program issues, etc
Support production recovery events including robot resynchronization and program restoration
Conduct structured RCA for repeating robot failures

Tooling (EOAT) Integration



Support end-of-arm tooling design reviews, integration, and change management
Troubleshoot EOAT issues etc

Robot Safety Support



Support robot safety validation activities
Ensure safety configurations, light curtains, and interlocks are maintained and validated

HV Safety & Compliance



Enforce HV LOTO, HVIL continuity, and mandatory HV PPE for all work on or near EV Powertrain equipment
Comply with SASO, IEC 60204, and functional safety standards (ISO 13849 / IEC 62061)
Support HV emergency response including thermal runaway isolation and battery-related incident procedures
Achieve and maintain HV safety competency appropriate to scope of work

Launch Governance & Ramp-Up



Support AMP-2 Safe Launch activities, run-at-rate events, and capacity verification within scope
Contribute to Launch Readiness Reviews, Layered Process Audits, and Process Confirmation routines
Participate in QRQC / RCCA escalations during launch and ramp-up phases

Robot Application Engineering & Validation



Develop maintainable robot programs, frames, TCPs, payload data, zones, mastering, backups and recovery standards; validate path accuracy and cycle repeatability.
Integrate EOAT, vision, conveyors, safety PLC handshakes, process equipment and MES/traceability signals; confirm failure-mode recovery and restart behavior.
Execute reach, collision, singularity and cycle-time studies using RoboGuide, RobotStudio or KUKA.Sim and verify results on equipment.
Maintain controlled robot/EOAT backups, revision history, spare strategy and preventive-maintenance inputs.

Launch Governance, Change Control & Operational Readiness



Support FAT/SAT, commissioning, equipment acceptance, Safe Launch, run-at-rate and capacity verification with objective evidence and disciplined punch-list closure.
Control production, process, software and test changes through documented risk assessment, approvals, validation, revision history and rollback or containment planning.
Participate in readiness reviews, Layered Process Audits, Process Confirmation and QRQC/RCCA; close assigned actions with verified effectiveness.

Safety, Quality, Data Integrity & Compliance



Apply role-specific HV LOTO/HVIL, machine safety, stored-energy isolation, electrical safe-work and PPE requirements; never bypass safety devices or product protections.
Protect product genealogy, calibrated-tool status, test/measurement integrity, document control and audit-ready objective evidence.
Comply with applicable AMP-2, SASO, Saudi labor/EHS, IATF 16949, IEC 60204 and functional-safety requirements within assigned scope.

Saudization, Capability Transfer & Collaboration



Build Saudi national capability through structured OJT, skills matrices, practical assessment, certification, cross-training and documented knowledge transfer.
Create technical standards, troubleshooting guides and training material
Collaborate across Production, Quality, Maintenance, Automation/Robotics, Manufacturing Engineering, EHS, IT/OT, MES, Supply Chain, Product Engineering and suppliers.





 






Skills





Strong hands-on robotics programming skills (FANUC, ABB, etc)
Working knowledge of robot safety standards
Structured troubleshooting mindset
Effective communicator in bilingual (English/Arabic) technical environments
Technical standards, structured problem solving, risk-based decision making and controlled documentation
Data literacy: KPI definition, trend analysis, evidence-based validation and clear executive/shop-floor communication
Cross-functional influence, supplier coordination and disciplined ownership in a greenfield launch environment
Coaching, competency assessment and knowledge transfer in a multicultural English/Arabic workplace





 






Minimum Qualifications


 





Bachelor's degree in Mechatronics, Electrical, or Robotics Engineering
3+ years in industrial robotics
Hands-on programming experience with FANUC, ABB, or KUKA
Fluent in English; Arabic strongly preferred
Preferred: multi-brand robotics experience; EOAT integration; greenfield launch experience

Preferred Qualifications



Demonstrated experience with commissioning, FAT/SAT, launch, production readiness or high-volume manufacturing ramp within the role discipline

Lean/Six Sigma, greenfield EV/automotive launch and workforce-development experience
